concerns.text: The plan computes Hedges’ g using only post‑intervention means, SDs, and sample sizes (FR‑004, FR‑013). Relying solely on post‑scores ignores baseline measurements, which can bias effect‑size estimates if randomization does not perfectly balance groups. In psychological meta‑analyses it is standard to use change‑score data (pre‑post differences) or, when unavailable, to adjust for baseline imbalance. The current approach may therefore produce systematically inflated or deflated pooled effects, jeopardizing the validity of hypothesis tests (H1‑H4).
